song.title: If You Want Me To Stay

guitar.evidence: Freddie Stone (Sly's brother) played guitar in the band, but no singular iconic signature instrument is widely documented for the act.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with low confidence.

tone.target: dry funky rhythm clean with percussive attack
tone.profile: dry funky rhythm clean with percussive attack
tone.summary: The chain uses Comp for tight attack, followed by a low-gain US Deluxe amp model paired with the US 2x12 cab to achieve a bright, punchy, and dry sound suitable for funky rhythm playing.

rig.name: Sly And The Family Stone - If You Want Me To Stay - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight rhythm definition.
Provide slight compression and enhance the percussive attack required for funk rhythm.
Keep the signal clean and low-gain to maintain funk clarity.
Simulate a clean, bright small combo amp (Fender style) suitable for funk rhythm.
Provide a bright and punchy cabinet sound matching the small combo aesthetic.
Boost the upper mids and treble for brightness while slightly cutting bass to maintain tightness.
Avoid the wah effect as per the musical verdict.
Avoid chorus/tremolo effects to keep the tone dry and focused.
Avoid delay effects to maintain the dry funk sound.
Add minimal ambient space without sounding lush or muddy.
blocks.gap: The verdict asks to avoid 'lush reverb', so the mix and decay are kept very low/short.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for better funk punch and clarity.

proposals.reason: Enhance the vintage, tight punch required for funk rhythm.
